comment_data.body: @padasodo82 is this a malware?

> @padasodo82 is this a malware?

Sure looks like it! Scary. Unfortunately I don't have the permissions to delete or hide it, but I did report the account.

---

Out of curiosity, how slow is your internet connection? From a quick scan of the code, it seems like this should only happen if downloading updates takes more than 120 seconds.

> Out of curiosity, how slow is your internet connection? From a quick scan of the code, it seems like this should only happen if downloading updates takes more than 120 seconds.

Yes, it most certainly is. More importantly, @nickkadutskyi, does timeout indeed happen after (more or less) 2 minutes? If it does, then this is an expected behavior. The only solution *right now* is to run `:packupdate` again: either without arguments or in smaller, manually set batches (like update first 10 plugins, then another 10, and so on).

---

I do support adding custom timeout, but [it might not align with long term vision](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/34772#issuecomment-4826062786) of making any `vim.system()` call interruptible by `<C-c>` (which would not need a timeout).

Since I think having a hard timeout is important and all downloading is done in parallel, the current situation is the best I can think of. Having a "dynamic" total value that depends on the number of plugins is not ideal since it severely increases the timeout in case of many plugins. The better solution might be to have a (smaller) fixed timeout per single parallel job, but that requires adjusting `vim._async` which I'd like to avoid.

> The only solution _right now_ is to run `:packupdate` again

that seems like a reasonable workaround, and could be mentioned in the error message

> > The only solution _right now_ is to run `:packupdate` again
> 
> that seems like a reasonable workaround, and could be mentioned in the error message

Not *quite* possible without touching `vim._async`. The least invasive approach is to [add new `errmsg` argument](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/6a6431cb99f411a85ffb3157023cd4726614485d/runtime/lua/vim/_async.lua#L49) that would be used precisely on every `:wait`. Does that sound good?

> Having a "dynamic" total value that depends on the number of plugins is not ideal since it severely increases the timeout in case of many plugins.

What exactly is wrong with this? This sounds like ideal behavior to me.

> > Having a "dynamic" total value that depends on the number of plugins is not ideal since it severely increases the timeout in case of many plugins.
> 
> What exactly is wrong with this? This sounds like ideal behavior to me.

It is not ideal because there are cases when it doesn't deliver ideal behavior.

For example, let's use this issue's 39 plugins as an example. If there is a simple `timeout_per_plugin = 30000`, then it means that the total timeout for execution of all 39 plugins will be 19.5 minutes. Which is *a lot*. And if it is only 1 plugin, the timeout is 30 seconds, which proved to be *not a lot*.

Now, computing it something like `math.max(120000, 39 * 30000)` or `30000 * 39 / n_parallel` already feels like adding unnecessary complexity and a more fundamental solution is in order. Which is either a configurable total timeout or using a timeout per `vim.system()` call (and not for total joined parallel execution).

Let's not spend any more time on this.  

We have a path to allow `[count]<c-c>` to cancel tasks. If it really bothers people, anyone is free to work on making `[count]<c-c>` work. Otherwise, just wait.

@superatomic 
My internet speed is about 250 Mbps, also tried on different Mac in the same network and also in another network and I get the same issue.

@echasnovski 
> does timeout indeed happen after (more or less) 2 minutes?

I would say so

> The only solution right now is to run :packupdate again: either without arguments or in smaller, manually set batches (like update first 10 plugins, then another 10, and so on).

I've tried to do that for first 14 plugins but I always get this issue. I would run `vim.pack._get_names`, get first 13 plugins and then provide it to `vim.pack.update`, 13 always works fine but 14 would always timeout.

E.g. I would do this:
```lua
    vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>mu", function()
        local start_ind = 11
        local end_ind = 15
        local plugins = vim.pack._get_names()
        local to_update = {}
        for i = start_ind, math.min(end_ind, #plugins) do
            table.insert(to_update, plugins[i])
        end
        vim.notify("Updating plugins " .. table.concat(to_update, ", "))

        vim.pack.update(to_update)
    end, { silent = true, desc = "Plugins: plugin [m]anager [u]pdate" })
```
It would stuck on this batch. It seems like there is one specific plugin that makes it to wait too much time every time it tries to update it.

> My internet speed is about 250 Mbps ... 13 always works fine but 14 would always timeout

Do we have enough logging so that users can understand why something is waiting or failing?

I've just tried to update a small batch and stuck again. here are the plugins it tried to update: I ran it multiple times and maybe on 5th it went through, but there weren't any plugins requiring and update. Another test I've done: I ran `vim.pack.update` on all plugins in batches of 5 and it went fine and then I ran `:packupdate` on all plugins but it got timeouted and I see the same issue for vim.pack.update on all plugins. Another test: I ran `vim.pack.update` in batches of 5 and actually updated plugins and then ran `:packupdate` or `vim pack.update` on all plugins and it always gets timeouted. Running `vim.pack.update` on batch of 5 is done in no more than couple seconds. I have 39 plugins and all of the git fetch is supposed to be async so it's not supposed to timeout if I run update on all plugins? @justinmk > Do we have enough logging so that users can understand why something is waiting or failing? Would be useful to know which async job got timeouted.

> My internet speed is about 250 Mbps, also tried on different Mac in the same network and also in another network and I get the same issue.
> ...
> I've tried to do that for first 14 plugins but I always get this issue. I would run `vim.pack._get_names`, get first 13 plugins and then provide it to `vim.pack.update`, 13 always works fine but 14 would always timeout.

This is a very strange behavior that I both can't replicate and don't know why it might happen. I have about 50 Mpbs speed which can install or update 45 plugins in under five seconds. It is done in parallel batches of 24 (which is an expected `2 * vim.uv.available_parallelism()`).

Just to be sure, what is the output of `:=vim.uv.available_parallelism()`?

> It would stuck on this batch. It seems like there is one specific plugin that makes it to wait too much time every time it tries to update it.

Well, then narrowing down the plugin will probably locate the issue and would help a lot.

Also, did you try to delete (or move to other directory) all plugins and re-install them to see if this fix things?

---

> I have 39 plugins and all of the git fetch is supposed to be async so it's not supposed to timeout if I run update on all plugins?

@nickkadutskyi, does the timeout happen after around 2 minutes? If not, what is the approximate wall time until timeout (please make sure that the machine's processes are as clean as possible, i.e. not other active Git processes)?

---

> Do we have enough logging so that users can understand why something is waiting or failing?

If there is only one problematic plugin, then it is probably somewhere in the rest of 8 plugins. And the timeout actually does what it is designed to do: stop something that will get stuck forever.

For what it's worth, I am able to install and update all (40) plugins from [this lockfile](https://github.com/nickkadutskyi/nvim/blob/main/nvim-pack-lock.json).
could be a region-blocking issue or firewall depending on which country you live in, etc. who knows, the internet is... patchy, these days :)

8

> Also, did you try to delete (or move to other directory) all plugins and re-install them to see if this fix things?

It got stuck until that timeout error and then I restarted neovim but it didn't attempt to install plugins again so I got some errors due to missing plugins.

I was tinkering with my network, tried to run it through mobile internet tethering and it didn't work, but then I switched back to my home wifi and it works now. 

@justinmk 
> could be a region-blocking issue or firewall depending on which country you live in, etc. who knows, the internet is... patchy, these days :)

I thought about this and I ran `vim.pack.update` for small batches 10-20 times in row and it went fine, and now I am running update for all the plugins 10 times in a row and it's fine. Unless there is some rate limiter on Github that applies based on schedule and I wasn't lucky.

Currently, it works on my MacBook Air but doesn't work on Mac mini. They are both in the same network.

This is definitely not a network issue then.

I also copied `.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core` dir from Mac mini to MacBook air and it still works on MacBook Air
might be a git issue. in any case ... extending the timeout would have not solved anything here
What's your git versions between the two computers?

```

git version 2.54.0
```
Yeah, that's up to date (enough at least; mine is 2.55.0). And regardless, the versions are the same. Hmm.... I'm not sure what could be wrong.

> Currently, it works on my MacBook Air but doesn't work on Mac mini. They are both in the same network.
>

Well, I am no expert in the area, but I'd guess it still might be. Maybe the Mac mini device did something when GitHub was in a bad mood and somehow limited the activity per device. Maybe through token or some other dark magic.

In any case, I indeed don't think this is a `vim.pack` issue and timeout here did its job pretty well (otherwise, the whole Neovim would be blocked indefinitely).

I took my MBA to another place with completely different network (though the same ISP) and ran `vim.pack.update` multiple times and it did well. Then I restarted the Mac and update stuck every time.
